DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_HUD
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: In-game HUD overlay. Comma-separated list of elements to display.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_FRAME_RATE
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc:
Frame rate limiter. 0 = uncapped. Positive value limits to N FPS.
REMOVED in upstream DXVK 3.0 — the variable is no longer read there. Still honoured by DXVK <= 2.7 and forks such as dxvk-low-latency. On DXVK 3.x use DXVK_CONFIG="dxvk.maxFrameRate = 60" instead, or an external limiter (gamescope -r, MangoHud, vk_flip_meter).

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_LOG_LEVEL
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls message logging verbosity.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_LOG_PATH
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Directory path for DXVK log files (app_d3d11.log, app_dxgi.log etc.).

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_SHADER_DUMP_PATH
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Dump compiled shader bytecode to this directory for debugging.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_SHADER_CACHE_PATH
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Override the shader pipeline state cache directory.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_STATE_CACHE
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: [Legacy] Pipeline state cache control. Set to 0 to disable. Not read by current upstream DXVK (the state cache is gone; DXVK 3.x caches compiled shaders instead — see DXVK_SHADER_CACHE). Kept for older builds and DXVK-Sarek (1.10-based).

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_STATE_CACHE_PATH
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: [Legacy] Directory for pipeline state cache files. Same caveat as DXVK_STATE_CACHE — use DXVK_SHADER_CACHE_PATH on DXVK 3.x.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Select GPU by substring match on Vulkan device name.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_UUID
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Select GPU by 32-char hex Vulkan device UUID (no dashes).

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_HDR
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable HDR10 color space exposure (DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_FULL_G2084). Needed by some HDR-capable games.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NO_HDR
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS / Proton-EM] Opposite of DXVK_HDR=1: forcefully disables HDR when it would otherwise be switched on automatically (current Protons detect HDR by themselves). Useful on GNOME, which does not yet expose enough colour-management features for DXVK's HDR path.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_DEBUG
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc:
Enables one DXVK debugging mode.
capture: debug names and markers for render passes/shaders (default under some capture tools).
hang: detects GPU hangs / VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and logs the failing command(s) — attach the log to bug reports.
markers: forwards application-provided resource names and markers via VK_EXT_debug_utils.
validation: enables the validation callback; also needs VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_CAPTURE_FRAMES
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Triggers a frame capture (RenderDoc) for a range of frames: 'first' or 'first:count'. E.g. 500:3 captures frames 500-502. Malformed values are logged and ignored. Debugging only.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_ASYNC
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Async shader compilation (unofficial/patched builds). 1 = enable.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable Vulkan instance layers. Use VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation for debug.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_ENABLE_NVAPI
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable NVAPI support. Required for DLSS, Reflex, and MFG.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NUM_COMPILER_THREADS
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc:
Number of pipeline compiler threads. 0 = use all available CPU cores; a positive number enforces that exact thread count. Some threads are reserved for high-priority work when the graphics pipeline library feature is enabled. Set to 1 to force fully single-threaded shader compilation (deterministic, but slower cold-start compiles).
Note: upstream DXVK 3.x does not read this variable — use DXVK_CONFIG="dxvk.numCompilerThreads = N" there.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_CONFIG_FILE
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Overrides the path DXVK searches for its dxvk.conf. By default DXVK looks for dxvk.conf in the working directory (usually the game's exe folder). Useful for keeping a shared config outside a Windows-only game folder.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_CONFIG
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc:
Sets one or more dxvk.conf keys directly through the environment instead of a config file, using the same key = value syntax, with ; as a separator between entries. Any key documented in dxvk.conf can be set this way (dxgi.*, d3d9.*, d3d11.*, dxvk.*), e.g. dxgi.maxFrameLatency, dxgi.hideNvidiaGpu, dxvk.enableGraphicsPipelineLibrary, d3d11.samplerAnisotropy. Takes priority over an on-disk dxvk.conf for the keys it sets.
The picker below covers the latency/Reflex, present, pipeline, NVIDIA and filtering keys from upstream dxvk.conf; any other key goes into 'Other entries' and is kept verbatim.

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_WSI_DRIVER
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Selects the windowing backend DXVK talks to. On Linux builds this is NOT optional — DXVK throws DxvkError("DXVK_WSI_DRIVER environment variable unset") when it is empty, since only the Win32 build has a sane fallback. Proton and Lutris set it for you; you only touch it when running DXVK outside a launcher, or to force SDL3 vs SDL2 while chasing a fullscreen/HDR/cursor bug. The value must match a backend that was actually compiled in, otherwise WSI init fails outright. Syntax: DXVK_WSI_DRIVER=SDL3 %command%

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NO_VR
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Stops DXVK from loading and querying OpenVR. DXVK asks OpenVR which Vulkan instance/device extensions a VR runtime needs; on a machine with SteamVR installed but no headset in use that probe can cost startup time or hang if the runtime is in a bad state. Set to 1 for non-VR games on a VR-capable system. Syntax: DXVK_NO_VR=1 %command%

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_FORCE_WINDOWED
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Forces D3D9 swapchains to stay windowed, ignoring the game's request for exclusive fullscreen. Useful for old D3D9 titles that mode-switch badly on Wayland or on a multi-monitor setup, and for keeping a compositor's VRR / HDR path in charge instead of handing the display over to the game. D3D9 path only. Syntax: DXVK_FORCE_WINDOWED=1 %command%

DXVK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_SHADER_CACHE
DXVK_ENV_VARS.desc: Set to 0 to disable the driver-level shader cache DXVK enables by default (only checked when no shader dump path is set). Distinct from DXVK_STATE_CACHE, which is DXVK's own pipeline state cache. Mostly a debugging switch — disabling it means every run pays full compilation cost. Syntax: DXVK_SHADER_CACHE=0 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_CONFIG
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma/semicolon-separated list of behavior flags for vkd3d-proton.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_FRAME_RATE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Frame rate limiter. 0 = uncapped. Positive value = limit to N FPS.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_DEBUG
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Debug log verbosity for vkd3d-proton runtime.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_DEBUG
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Debug log verbosity for shader compilers.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_LOG_FILE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Redirect VKD3D_DEBUG log output to this file.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_VULKAN_DEVICE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Zero-based Vulkan device index to force device selection.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Skip Vulkan devices that don't contain this substring.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_DISABLE_EXTENSIONS
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma-separated list of Vulkan extensions to disable.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_CACHE_PATH
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Override directory for vkd3d-proton.cache. Set to '0' to disable.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_DUMP_PATH
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Dump shader bytecode (SPIR-V/DXBC/DXIL) to this directory.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_OVERRIDE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Directory containing override SPIR-V shaders by hash.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_PRESENT_MODE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Force a specific Vulkan present mode for the swapchain.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_DESCRIPTOR_QA_LOG
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Path to log descriptor heap operations. Requires descriptor_qa build.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_DEBUG_RING_SIZE_LOG2
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Log2 size in bytes of the shader printf debug ring buffer (e.g. 28 = 256 MiB).

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_LATENCY_FRAMES
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc:
Maximum number of frames in flight, enforced through KHR_present_wait (default 3). Lower = less input lag at the cost of CPU/GPU starvation risk; 2 is often stable, 1 is aggressive. Also accepted on the DXGI path. Default removed in v2.14 (was previously forced to 2).
Upstream applies it to the swapchain's internal frame latency, accepting 1 up to the DXGI swap-chain buffer maximum.
vkd3d-low-latency ALSO feeds it to the frame pacer's wait latency, and there only 1-3 is accepted. That fork deliberately defaults to 3 rather than dxvk-low-latency's 2: at 2 a lot of D3D12 games throttle their fps, so 2 is left as a manual choice for the titles where it doesn't. Syntax: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_LATENCY_FRAMES=2 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_LIMIT_TESS_FACTORS
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Clamp tessellation factors to reduce GPU load in titles with excessive tessellation (e.g. Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty). 0 = disabled (default). Automatically enabled for known problematic games.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_FEATURE_LEVEL
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Force the reported D3D12 feature level, regardless of what the Vulkan driver would otherwise expose. Useful for games that refuse to start when they detect a feature level they don't expect, or that under-report driver capability.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_WORKER_THREAD_COUNT
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Number of background worker threads vkd3d-proton uses for shader/pipeline compilation and pipeline-library disk-cache I/O. Fewer threads reduce CPU contention from compile storms on busy many-core systems; more can speed up cold-cache compile bursts at the cost of using more cores at once.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_PIPELINE_LIBRARY_SIZE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Caps the size (in bytes) of the automatic vkd3d-proton.cache pipeline library vkd3d-proton maintains on disk. Once the cap is hit, older/least-used entries are evicted rather than letting the cache grow without bound.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_PIPELINE_LIBRARY_APP_CACHE_ONLY
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Restrict pipeline caching to whatever the application itself explicitly manages through ID3D12PipelineLibrary, instead of also letting vkd3d-proton silently cache every PSO it sees in its own automatic vkd3d-proton.cache disk cache.

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_IMAGES
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Overrides the swapchain's minimum image count. The driver minimum is still respected, so this can only raise it. More images smooth over presentation hitches at the cost of latency and VRAM; fewer is not achievable this way. Syntax: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_IMAGES=3 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_DEBUG_LATENCY
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Logs per-present latency information from the swapchain. Diagnostic — pair with PROTON_LOG=1 when checking whether a game actually drives the low-latency path at all. Syntax: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_DEBUG_LATENCY=1 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_MODEL
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Caps the shader model vkd3d-proton reports to the game. Lowering it can steer a title onto a simpler rendering path (or work around a broken SM6.6+ path); raising it above what the driver supports will not work. Unrecognised strings are ignored. Syntax: VKD3D_SHADER_MODEL=6_6 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_LOG_BUFFERED
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Buffers log output in memory instead of writing it out line by line; the value is the ring buffer size in bytes. Keeps heavy VKD3D_DEBUG logging from distorting the very frame timings you are trying to measure. Note the trade-off: on a hard crash the tail of the log may never be flushed. Syntax: VKD3D_LOG_BUFFERED=1048576 VKD3D_DEBUG=info %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_UNIX_ENV
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Passes environment variables from the Unix side into the D3D12 core module at load time (applied early, before device creation). Escape hatch for launchers that cannot set a variable in the Wine environment directly. Syntax: VKD3D_UNIX_ENV="VKD3D_CONFIG=dxr" %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_UNIX_POST_ENV
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Same mechanism as VKD3D_UNIX_ENV but applied LATE in initialisation, for settings that must not be visible during early setup. Syntax: VKD3D_UNIX_POST_ENV="..." %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Writes a queue timeline trace to the given path — submissions, waits and signals per Vulkan queue. The tool of choice when frametime spikes look like queue starvation or a serialised submit rather than raw GPU cost. Syntax: VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE=/tmp/queue.json %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE_ABSOLUTE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Emits queue-profile timestamps as absolute values instead of relative ones, so the trace lines up with Wine's QPC-relative logs. Only meaningful together with VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE. Syntax: VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE=/tmp/q.json VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE_ABSOLUTE=1 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_TIMESTAMP_PROFILE
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Writes GPU timestamp profiling data to the given path — per-pass GPU cost, as opposed to VKD3D_QUEUE_PROFILE's submission-level view. Syntax: VKD3D_TIMESTAMP_PROFILE=/tmp/ts.json %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_PROFILE_PATH
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Output path for vkd3d-proton's built-in profiling counters (enabled in builds compiled with profiling support). Syntax: VKD3D_PROFILE_PATH=/tmp/vkd3d-profile %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_AUTO_CAPTURE_SHADER
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: RenderDoc auto-capture: captures the frame in which the shader with this hash is used. Requires the RenderDoc layer to be loaded; vkd3d warns and does nothing when neither this nor VKD3D_AUTO_CAPTURE_COUNTS is set. Syntax: VKD3D_AUTO_CAPTURE_SHADER=<hash> %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_AUTO_CAPTURE_COUNTS
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: RenderDoc auto-capture by frame number — a comma-separated list of frame indices to capture. Can be used on its own or alongside VKD3D_AUTO_CAPTURE_SHADER. Syntax: VKD3D_AUTO_CAPTURE_COUNTS=100,200,300 %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_QA_HASHES
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Path to a file of shader hashes for descriptor QA / validation runs. Note the side effect: setting this (like VKD3D_SHADER_OVERRIDE or VKD3D_SHADER_DUMP_PATH) forces the pipeline_library_ignore_spirv config flag on, so the pipeline library stops being reused — expect slower startup while it is set. Syntax: VKD3D_QA_HASHES=/tmp/hashes.txt %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_BARRIER_HASHES
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Path to a file of shader hashes used by the breadcrumb/barrier debugging path, for narrowing a GPU hang down to specific barriers. Debug only. Syntax: VKD3D_BARRIER_HASHES=/tmp/barriers.txt %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_SHADER_QUIRKS
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Path to a file of per-shader quirk overrides, applied at shader compile time. Development aid for testing a workaround before it is baked into vkd3d-proton's own quirk tables. Syntax: VKD3D_SHADER_QUIRKS=/tmp/quirks.txt %command%

VKD3D_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_BLOOM_BUFFER_SIZE_LOG2
VKD3D_ENV_VARS.desc: Size of the descriptor-QA bloom filter buffer, as a power of two (24 = 16 MiB, the default). Only allocated when descriptor QA with sync validation is active; raise it if the QA layer reports collisions. Syntax: VKD3D_BLOOM_BUFFER_SIZE_LOG2=26 %command%

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_ALLOW_UNOFFICIAL_PROTOCOL
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Allows the NVIDIA GLX client to use 'unofficial' GLX protocol extensions for OpenGL features beyond v1.5. Requires NVIDIA GLX libraries on both client and server.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_FORCE_INDIRECT
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Forces the NVIDIA OpenGL driver to use indirect GLX rendering — sends GL commands over the network to an X server. Workaround for certain compatibility issues. (1 = enable)

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_DISALLOW_SOFTWARE_FALLBACK
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Prevents the OpenGL driver from falling back to software rendering when hardware acceleration fails.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_NO_DSO_FINALIZER
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Workaround for multithreaded OpenGL apps: forces libGL's DSO finalizer to leave resources in place on exit so other threads can still call OpenGL safely. OS reclaims all memory when the process terminates.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_WRITE_TEXT_SECTION
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls whether the NVIDIA OpenGL driver can write to executable memory sections. Set to 0 to disable this optimization — workaround for segfaults in some apps.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_IGNORE_GLSL_EXT_REQS
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Ignores certain GLSL extension requirements. Useful workaround for specific games such as Dying Light. (1 = enable)

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_YIELD
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies what the NVIDIA OpenGL driver does when it needs to yield CPU time. USLEEP changes the yielding behavior to usleep(). Workaround for scheduling problems.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SYNC_DISPLAY_DEVICE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies which display connector to synchronize rendering to (VSync target). Use in multi-monitor setups to eliminate tearing. Also works with Vulkan apps. Example values: HDMI-0, DP-4, DVI-D-0

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Overrides the directory path for the NVIDIA OpenGL shader disk cache. By default the cache lives in ~/.nv. Useful to redirect to faster storage or a shared location across users.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_APP_NAME
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies an application name for the shader disk cache, creating app-specific cache entries. Prevents cache key collisions between different applications.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_READ_ONLY
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Makes the shader disk cache read-only. When set, the driver will not write new compiled shader entries to the cache — useful for locked/shared deployments.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_READ_ONLY_APP_NAME
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies an application name for a read-only shader disk cache. Used in conjunction with __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_READ_ONLY.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SKIP_CLEANUP
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Prevents the NVIDIA driver from cleaning up (evicting) old shader disk cache entries. Can help reduce shader compilation stuttering by keeping all cached shaders intact. (1 = skip cleanup)

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHARPEN_ALLOW
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Allows the NVIDIA Image Sharpening feature to be used by this process. Must be enabled before __GL_SHARPEN_ENABLE takes effect.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHARPEN_ENABLE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables NVIDIA Image Sharpening for OpenGL and Vulkan games. Improves clarity and sharpness. Available since driver 441.41. Requires __GL_SHARPEN_ALLOW=1.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHARPEN_VALUE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls the sharpening strength. Higher values produce a stronger effect. Typical range 0–100.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHARPEN_IGNORE_FILM_GRAIN
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls whether the sharpening filter ignores film grain effects. Prevents the sharpening pass from accentuating synthetic film grain noise.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHARPEN_INDICATOR_ENABLE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Shows an on-screen indicator when NVIDIA Image Sharpening is active.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_LOG_MAX_ANISO
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables automatic anisotropic texture filtering for OpenGL: 0 = none, 1 = 2x, 2 = 4x, 3 = 8x, 4 = 16x.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_ALLOW_FXAA_USAGE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Set to 0 to let an individual application opt out of FXAA when FXAA is enabled globally in nvidia-settings.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_HEAP_ALLOC_LIMIT
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Per-process limit on the driver's heap allocations, written as BYTES with an optional case-insensitive suffix (k, kB, M, MB, G, GB); no suffix = bytes. Values below 12 MB are clamped up to 12 MB.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_ConformantBlitFramebufferScissor
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: glBlitFramebuffer() scissor test: enabled by default (spec-conformant). Set 0 to disable it for old applications that relied on the previous behaviour.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SORT_FBCONFIGS
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Set to 0 to return GLX FBConfigs in the order the X server reports them instead of the driver's sorted order.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHOW_GRAPHICS_OSD
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Shows an on-screen display (OSD) indicator for the graphics API currently in use. Can also be set via nvidia-settings or an application profile.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_APPLICATION_PROFILE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies an application profile name to load. Application profiles override global and base profile settings. The driver loads these on process init.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SELINUX_BOOLEANS
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls SELinux policy detection for the NVIDIA OpenGL driver. Some fallback allocation methods may be prohibited under SELinux; this variable allows manual override of the detection.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_MAYA_OPTIMIZE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables/disables OpenGL optimizations for Autodesk Maya. The NVIDIA Linux driver 295.59 disabled certain OpenGL optimizations that affect Maya performance. Set to 1 to re-enable if you experience performance loss.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_EVENT_LOGFILE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies a file path for NVIDIA OpenGL event logging. Used for debugging and troubleshooting by NVIDIA support.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_EVENT_LOGLEVEL
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls the verbosity level of NVIDIA OpenGL event logging. TRACE is most verbose; OFF disables logging entirely.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_EXPERT_DETAIL_LEVEL
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Controls the level of detail for GLExpert debugging output. GLExpert is part of the instrumented driver providing real-time OpenGL runtime info. Higher values produce more detailed output.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_EXPERT_OUTPUT_MASK
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Bitmask controlling where GLExpert debugging output is sent (e.g. console, stdout, debugger). Used together with __GL_EXPERT_REPORT_MASK.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_EXPERT_REPORT_MASK
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Bitmask filtering which types of GLExpert debugging reports are generated. Used together with __GL_EXPERT_OUTPUT_MASK.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_DEBUG_FILENAME
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Specifies a filename for debug trace output from the NVIDIA OpenGL driver. Used in conjunction with __GL_DEBUG to redirect trace output.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_FIX_VIEWPERF2020_BUFFER_NAME_BUG
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Fixes a specific bug in SPEC Viewperf 2020 benchmarks related to buffer naming. Viewperf data sets are GL API traces from CAD apps; the bug caused rendering to appear darker than expected.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_DOOM3
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Legacy variable for the Doom 3 game. A driver bug (fixed in 319.32) caused crashes when this was set. Kept here for reference; not needed on modern drivers.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_13ebad
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: idTech engine VRAM placement workaround. Tells the NVIDIA Vulkan driver to override application-requested memory locations and force performance-critical resources into video memory. First needed for Doom Eternal (2020), later confirmed for Indiana Jones and the Great Circle (Dec 2024). Workaround confirmed by an NVIDIA engineer on the developer forum; planned for auto-enablement in a future driver release. Only effective on idTech-based games with the proprietary NVIDIA Linux Vulkan driver. Steam launch options: __GL_13ebad=0x1 %command%

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_MaxFramesAllowed
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Caps how many frames the OpenGL driver will queue ahead of the display (pre-rendered frames). Defaults to 2. Set to 1 for the Linux equivalent of Windows' NVIDIA 'Low Latency Mode: On' — noticeably reduces input lag and frame-pacing jitter in compositors/games that rely on it. 0 aims for the 'Ultra' equivalent but is reported to not fully work on Linux.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Offloads some of the OpenGL driver's CPU-side work to a separate worker thread. Helps CPU-bound OpenGL titles; can hurt titles that make heavy synchronous calls like glGet*. Requires the app to link pthreads (use LD_PRELOAD=libpthread.so.0 if it doesn't). Enabled by default under some conditions with self-disable if it isn't helping; this forces it on.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SYNC_TO_VBLANK
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Classic OpenGL VSync toggle. 0 lets glXSwapBuffers return immediately without waiting for vblank (tearing possible, lowest latency); 1 (default) syncs every swap to the display's vertical refresh.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_GSYNC_ALLOWED
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Allows (1) or blocks (0) G-SYNC/variable refresh rate on a G-SYNC-capable display for OpenGL applications. NOTE: only affects OpenGL — Vulkan/DXVK/VKD3D-Proton titles ignore this entirely; VRR for those is controlled at the compositor/display-server level instead.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_VRR_ALLOWED
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Same G-SYNC/adaptive-sync allow/block toggle as __GL_GSYNC_ALLOWED, under the more generic 'VRR' name. Same OpenGL-only caveat applies — has no effect on Vulkan applications.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Master on/off switch for the NVIDIA OpenGL driver's shader disk cache. The other __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_* variables only take effect while this is on (on by default when a cache directory is resolvable).

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SIZE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Maximum size in bytes of the NVIDIA OpenGL shader disk cache. Once exceeded, older entries are evicted. Raise this if a big/long game library keeps thrashing the cache and causing re-compiles.

NV_ENV_VARS.name: __GL_FSAA_MODE
NV_ENV_VARS.desc: Forces a specific driver-level full-screen antialiasing mode, using the same integer values as `nvidia-settings --assign FSAA=N`. Run `nvidia-settings --query fsaa` to list the modes your GPU supports. Only takes effect for modes the app doesn't already control itself (see FSAAAppControlled).

NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.name: __NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD
NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.desc: On a hybrid laptop (iGPU driving the display, NVIDIA dGPU idle), forces the OpenGL/EGL side of an application to render on the NVIDIA GPU via PRIME render offload instead of the iGPU. Pair with __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia (System / Loader category) and __VK_LAYER_NV_optimus below for the Vulkan half. Directly relevant on this machine's Ryzen iGPU + RTX 4080 Mobile combo.

NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.name: __NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD_PROVIDER
NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.desc: Only needed with more than one discrete GPU to offload to: names the specific Xorg PRIME provider to render on, e.g. 'NVIDIA-G0'. Find yours with `xrandr --listproviders`. Leave unset on a normal single-dGPU laptop.

NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.name: __VK_LAYER_NV_optimus
NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.desc: Loads NVIDIA's Vulkan PRIME-offload layer so a Vulkan app actually picks the NVIDIA GPU. Needed because Vulkan apps otherwise just take the first device the loader enumerates, which on a hybrid laptop is often the iGPU. 'NVIDIA_only' is the value actually used, not a boolean.

NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.name: DRI_PRIME
NVIDIA_PRIME_ENV_VARS.desc: The Mesa-side equivalent PRIME offload switch (1 = use the secondary GPU, or a specific 'pci-xxxx_xx_xx_x' bus address). Mainly relevant here if you're running the open-source Nouveau driver on the RTX 4080 Mobile instead of the proprietary driver — has no effect on the proprietary NVIDIA driver path.

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: ENABLE_LAYER_cpu_flip_meter
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Activates the Vulkan implicit layer. This is the enable_environment key from the layer manifest; without it the layer stays inactive even if loaded. Syntax: ENABLE_LAYER_cpu_flip_meter=1 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: DISABLE_LAYER_cpu_flip_meter
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Globally disables the layer (e.g. to turn off a system-wide implicit layer for one specific game). Syntax: DISABLE_LAYER_cpu_flip_meter=1 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_MODE
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: v3.0: the layer configures itself — frame-generation multiplier, floor ratio, spin margin, hitch handling and FIFO fixed-refresh/VRR detection are all automatic. auto: FPS cap if FLM_TARGET_FPS>0, otherwise the floor pacer wherever it can help (presentWait + MAILBOX/IMMEDIATE, or FIFO whose measured cadence is VRR). latency: like auto with a looser floor and faster hitch recovery. present: like auto, but also paces FIFO swapchains judged fixed-refresh. cap: limiter only (needs FLM_TARGET_FPS). off: layer loaded but inactive (A/B baseline). The legacy FLM_PROFILE=vrr|mfg|latency|cap|off and FLM_MODE=limiter are still accepted as aliases. Hot-reloadable. Syntax: FLM_MODE=latency %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_TARGET_FPS
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: >0 = FPS cap (absolute-timeline limiter, no presentWait needed, works on every driver). 0 = natural cadence: the floor pacer smooths delivery without capping. Hot-reloadable. Syntax: FLM_TARGET_FPS=120 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_FLOOR_RATIO
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Optional override of the floor pacer's base ratio (500-1000; 1000 = one full slot). Unset = mode default (auto 850, latency 780). The closed loop still adjusts around it per frame-generation multiplier, and the ratchet guard still keeps the floor below the slot. Higher = flatter, lower = less held. Leave unset unless A/B data says otherwise. Hot-reloadable. Syntax: FLM_FLOOR_RATIO=900 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_MFG_MULTIPLIER
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Frame-generation multiplier. 0 = auto-detect (default; re-checked periodically, follows in-game changes). 1-4 = force. Load-time only. Syntax: FLM_MFG_MULTIPLIER=4 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_MEASURE_CPU
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: CPU affinity of the measurement thread — comma list of cores/ranges, e.g. '0-3,8'. Useful with CCD isolation. Load-time only. Syntax: FLM_MEASURE_CPU=0-3 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_RT_PRIORITY
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: SCHED_FIFO priority of the measurement thread (1-99, needs CAP_SYS_NICE). 0 = normal scheduling. Load-time only. Syntax: FLM_RT_PRIORITY=40 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_LOG_LEVEL
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Log verbosity (default WARN). INFO shows the resolved config, MFG multiplier changes and the FIFO/VRR verdict; DEBUG is near per-frame. Removed v2.x variables are reported once at WARN. Hot-reloadable. Syntax: FLM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_LOG_FILE
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Log file path (default stderr, which Steam/Lutris often swallow). Load-time only. Syntax: FLM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO FLM_LOG_FILE=/tmp/flm.log %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_STATS
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: 1 = summary line every 5 s at INFO: avg, p99, max interval, fake/hitch counts, detected multiplier, effective floor ratio (0 = pacer not running on this swapchain) and the FIFO verdict. Load-time only. Syntax: FLM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO FLM_STATS=1 %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_CSV
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: Per-flip measurement dump for A/B analysis (columns flip_ns, interval_ns, is_fake, is_hitch, slot, mfg, slot_mean_ns, pacing). Survives swapchain recreation (appends), flushed every 5 s. Load-time only. Syntax: FLM_MODE=off FLM_CSV=/tmp/off.csv %command%

FLM_ENV_VARS.name: FLM_CONFIG
FLM_ENV_VARS.desc: KEY=VALUE file re-read on SIGUSR1 for live tuning. Hot-reloadable keys: FLM_MODE, FLM_TARGET_FPS, FLM_FLOOR_RATIO, FLM_LOG_LEVEL (FLM_PROFILE alias too). Each reload starts from defaults → env → file, so deleting a line reverts it. Syntax: FLM_CONFIG=/tmp/flm.conf %command%  →  then: echo 'FLM_MODE=latency' > /tmp/flm.conf && kill -USR1 $(pgrep -f game)

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_NTSYNC
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Use the kernel-backed ntsync driver for Wine's in-process synchronization primitives instead of Esync/Fsync. Lower CPU overhead and more consistent timing than Fsync in titles that need it. On newer Proton-CachyOS/Valve Proton 11 builds ntsync is already the default and this variable has been removed there — use PROTON_NO_NTSYNC=1 on those builds to go back to Fsync.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_NTSYNC
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable ntsync (the default kernel sync driver on Proton 11 / current Proton-CachyOS) and fall back to Fsync. Useful for the rare title that misbehaves specifically under ntsync.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_ESYNC
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Do not use eventfd-based in-process synchronization primitives (disables Esync).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_FSYNC
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Do not use futex-based in-process synchronization primitives (disables Fsync). Automatically disabled anyway on systems without FUTEX_WAIT_MULTIPLE support.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_PRIORITY_HIGH
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Not part of any official Proton, Proton-CachyOS or Proton-GE variable table — no confirmed source reads this exact name. Community shorthand for 'give the game process a higher scheduling priority' is usually done via a launch wrapper (gamemoderun, CachyOS's game-performance) rather than an env var read by Proton itself. Kept here so the value is captured, but verify it actually does anything on your setup before relying on it.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_ENABLE_HDR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Legacy HDR toggle. Retired in current Proton-CachyOS in favour of DXVK_HDR (see the DXVK category), but Valve's stable Proton and most Proton-GE builds still read this name directly. Combine with ENABLE_HDR_WSI if needed.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: ENABLE_HDR_WSI
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables the HDR window-system-integration Vulkan extension path. Needed alongside DXVK_HDR/PROTON_ENABLE_HDR on NVIDIA driver versions older than 595.x, or together with a compositor-side HDR layer (e.g. vk-hdr-layer on KDE 6) when the compositor itself needs to be told HDR is coming.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable Wine's native winewayland.drv instead of XWayland/winex11.drv. Experimental — can improve latency and frame pacing and is required for HDR without Gamescope, but currently breaks the Steam Overlay and Steam Input in several builds. Alias: PROTON_USE_WAYLAND.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_HIDE_NVIDIA_GPU
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Force NVIDIA GPUs to always be reported as AMD GPUs. Some games require this if they depend on Windows-only NVIDIA driver functionality. See also DXVK's nvapiHack config, which only affects reporting from Direct3D.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_ENABLE_NVAPI
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable NVIDIA's NVAPI GPU support library inside the Wine prefix. Needed on older Proton (<= 9) and some forks. Valve Proton 10 copies nvapi64.dll into the prefix by default unless the game is marked 'disablenvapi' — there, use PROTON_FORCE_NVAPI=1 to override such a per-game block instead. Usually paired with PROTON_HIDE_NVIDIA_GPU=0.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DISABLE_NVAPI
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable NVIDIA's NVAPI GPU support library. Occasionally fixes crashes or low performance in titles that have buggy NVAPI code paths on Linux.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FORCE_NVAPI
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Proton 10: forces NVAPI on even for titles Proton disables it for by default (maps to the 'forcenvapi' compat flag, which wins over 'disablenvapi'). Use when DLSS/Reflex is missing in a game Proton blocks NVAPI for.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_HIDE_APU
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Hides an AMD APU's integrated GPU from the game (Proton sets WINE_HIDE_APU=1). On hybrid laptops (Ryzen iGPU + NVIDIA dGPU) this stops games that enumerate adapters from picking or mis-detecting the iGPU. Proton applies it automatically for a few titles (e.g. Deathloop).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_LIMIT_RESOLUTIONS
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Caps how many display modes Wine reports to the game. Some titles crash or misbehave with very long mode lists on high-refresh panels; Proton sets 16/32 automatically for e.g. Sekiro, Nier: Automata, Dark Souls III.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_CPU_TOPOLOGY
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Proton alias for WINE_CPU_TOPOLOGY ('N:i,j,k,...'); copied into WINE_CPU_TOPOLOGY by the Proton script. Useful for pinning a game to specific cores (e.g. one CCD / the V-Cache CCD).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVAPI_BYPASS
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Not a documented Proton/DXVK/VKD3D variable — no official source for this exact name was found. Most likely a mix-up with PROTON_DISABLE_NVAPI or DXVK_ENABLE_NVAPI (see the DXVK category). Kept here so the typed value is captured, but treat it as unconfirmed.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_ENABLE_NGX_UPDATER
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables NVIDIA's NGX Updater inside the Wine prefix, letting NGX Core download newer DLSS/DLSS-G DLLs at runtime instead of using the ones shipped with the game. This is the one-launch-option way to force a newer DLSS preset via DXVK_NVAPI_DRS_NGX_* (see DXVK-NVAPI category). Known to cause 2nd-run crashes in a few Unreal Engine titles — disable it again if that happens.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DLSS_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Automatically download and use a newer nvngx_dlss(d|g).dll than the one the game ships with. Set to 1 for the latest known-good version, or a specific version string (e.g. '310.2') to pin one. Also sets DXVK_NVAPI_DRS_SETTINGS to the latest preset unless you override it yourself.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable alternative NVIDIA library shims (nvcuda, nvenc, nvml, nvoptix) missing from stock Proton. Needed for things like hardware-accelerated PhysX. Only enable when a game actually needs it — incompatible with PROTON_USE_WOW64=1.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS_NO_32BIT
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Use together with PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS to restrict the shims to 64-bit only. Fixes bad performance/crashes on RTX 4000/5000-series cards when the 32-bit nvidia-libs shims get loaded for a 32-bit game.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVCUDA
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable only the alternative nvcuda.dll shim from nvidia-libs, without pulling in nvenc/nvml/nvoptix too. Narrower alternative to PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVENC
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable only the alternative NVENC hardware-encode shim from nvidia-libs. Relevant for in-game recording/streaming pipelines that call NVENC directly.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVML
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable only the NVML shim from nvidia-libs (GPU temperature/utilization queries). Lets in-game or overlay tools read real GPU stats. Enabled by default in Proton-CachyOS.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVOPTIX
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable only the OptiX ray-tracing shim from nvidia-libs. Needed by the rare title that uses NVIDIA OptiX directly rather than DXR/VKD3D-Proton's raytracing path.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DLSS_INDICATOR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Show a small on-screen DLSS status overlay confirming DLSS is actually active and which mode it's running in — the same overlay toggled by DXVK_NVAPI_SET_NGX_DEBUG_OPTIONS=DLSSIndicator=1024 (DXVK-NVAPI category), just as a one-flag shortcut.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_WINED3D
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Use OpenGL-based wined3d instead of Vulkan-based DXVK for d3d11/d3d10/d3d9. Rarely an improvement, but occasionally works around a DXVK-specific bug.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DXVK_SAREK
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [proton-cachyos] Switches the DXVK shipped with proton-cachyos over to DXVK-Sarek, a Vulkan 1.1/1.2 build maintained off the 1.10.x branch for GPUs that no longer meet upstream DXVK's requirements (and for Box64/FEX on Mali/Adreno). Sarek is the officially supported way to use it. On current hardware there is no reason to enable this — upstream DXVK is newer — except to reach Sarek-only options such as dyasync (DXVK_DISABLE_DYASYNC) or DXVK_ALL_CORES. Mutually exclusive in practice with PROTON_DXVK_LOWLATENCY: both replace the same DXVK. Syntax: PROTON_DXVK_SAREK=1 %command%

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DXVK_LOWLATENCY
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable the dxvk-low-latency fork (Proton-CachyOS/community builds), which adds low-latency frame pacing on top of DXVK to reduce input lag and improve frame pacing consistency. Mainly worth it in single-player titles.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DXVK_LLASYNC
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Not a documented Proton/Proton-CachyOS variable under this exact spelling. Most likely intended as PROTON_DXVK_LOWLATENCY (low-latency frame pacing) or the now-removed PROTON_DXVK_GPLASYNC (old async-compile patch). Kept here so the typed value is captured, but treat it as unconfirmed.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_VKD3D_HEAP
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Retired in current Proton-CachyOS with no replacement. Historically toggled an alternate vkd3d-proton heap allocation strategy. Kept here for older builds.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_LOCAL_SHADER_CACHE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable a per-game shader cache even when Steam's own 'Shader Pre-Caching' is off, mimicking it by keeping each game's cache under <steamlibrary>/shadercache/<appid>. Does not precompile shaders ahead of time — it only isolates each game's cache.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_PREFER_SDL
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Use SDL for controller input instead of HIDRAW/Steam Input. Can help controller detection issues under winewayland.drv. Alias: PROTON_USE_SDL.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_WM_DECORATION
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable window decorations drawn by the window manager, letting Wine draw its own decorations instead. Occasionally fixes windowed-mode focus/resize glitches.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FORCE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Force Wine to enable the LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE flag for all executables, letting 32-bit processes use more than 2 GiB of address space. Enabled by default.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_SET_GAME_DRIVE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Create an S: drive inside the Wine prefix pointing at the Steam library that contains the game. Some titles look for their install on a specific drive letter.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_ADD_CONFIG
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-EM / Proton-CachyOS] Comma-separated shortcut list that expands to several other variables at once, e.g. PROTON_ADD_CONFIG=wayland,ntsync is the same as setting PROTON_USE_WAYLAND=1 PROTON_USE_NTSYNC=1. Handy for combining several of the toggles above without a wall of launch options.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_WOW64
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [GE-Proton / Proton-EM / Proton-CachyOS, experimental] Run the game through Wine's newer WoW64 architecture (32-bit game, 64-bit Unix process via thunks) instead of a traditional 32-bit process. Some 32-bit titles report smoother frame timings with this on; others are still rough since it's experimental. Incompatible with PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_HEAP_DELAY_FREE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Delay freeing some memory instead of releasing it immediately, to work around application use-after-free bugs. A stability tweak more than a speed one, but avoids the stutter/crash a UAF bug would otherwise cause mid-game.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_LOG
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Dump a debug log to $PROTON_LOG_DIR/steam-$APPID.log. Set to 1 for the default WINEDEBUG channels, or a string to append extra channels to the default set. Proton's logging defaults (WINEDEBUG, DXVK_LOG_LEVEL, VKD3D_DEBUG …) only fill in vars that are unset — a leftover WINEDEBUG=-all gives an almost empty log.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_LOG_DIR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Directory to write PROTON_LOG output into. Defaults to your home directory.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DEBUG_DIR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Root directory Proton writes its per-game debug helper scripts into (proton_$USER/ subfolder, e.g. gdb_run for attaching a debugger). Defaults to /tmp. Only useful together with debugging workflows; has no effect on normal gameplay.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_EAC_RUNTIME
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Path to the 'Proton EasyAntiCheat Runtime' Steam depot, needed by some EAC-protected games that don't auto-detect it (install the runtime via Steam's 'Tools' category first, then point this at its folder). Usually not needed manually when the game's Steam depot already declares the dependency.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_BATTLEYE_RUNTIME
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Path to the 'Proton BattlEye Runtime' Steam depot, needed by some BattlEye-protected games that don't auto-detect it. Same idea as PROTON_EAC_RUNTIME — install the Steam Tools depot, then point here.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DXVK_D3D8
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Use DXVK's d3d8 implementation instead of wined3d for Direct3D 8 games.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_D3D10
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable d3d10 / d3d10_1 AND dxgi DLL overrides (blank override = not loaded). Forces games with another renderer to fall back to it.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_D3D11
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable the d3d11 DLL (blank override). Forces games with a D3D9/D3D12 renderer to pick another API.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_WINED3D11
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Use wined3d (OpenGL) for d3d11 only, keeping DXVK for the rest. Debug/compat.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Zero all Win32 heap allocations (sets WINE_HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY=1). Fixes crashes in games that read uninitialised heap memory; small CPU cost.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_LIMIT_ADDRESS_SPACE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Limit the process's usable virtual address space (read by Proton's Wine). Proton auto-sets it for AppIDs 1282270 and 2963870; try it for games that crash when given a very large address space.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_XALIA
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Xalia: controller-navigable UI for launchers/dialogs without gamepad support. Proton enables it by default (only for supported apps). Set 0 if it grabs input or adds an overlay you don't want.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DISABLE_HIDRAW
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma-separated VID/PID list of controllers that must NOT be exposed through hidraw (they fall back to SDL/evdev). Proton sets Sony DS4/DualSense IDs by default for some games.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_CRASH_REPORT_DIR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Write Wine crash reports (minidumps) to this directory (sets WINE_CRASH_REPORT_DIR).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FSR4_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS] Download amdxcffx64.dll and upgrade games that ship FSR 3.1 to FSR 4. 1 = default version from the upscaler manifest, or pin a version (e.g. 4.1.1). Opt-in. Needs a GPU/driver with FSR4 support — AMD RDNA3/4 only; it has no effect on an NVIDIA GPU (use PROTON_DLSS_UPGRADE there). Replaces the obsolete PROTON_FSR4_RDNA3_UPGRADE.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FSR4_INDICATOR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS] Show the FSR upscaling and frame-generation watermarks (shorthand for FSR_WATERMARK=1 and FSR_FG_WATERMARK=1).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FSR3_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Download and use a newer FSR 3.x FidelityFX DLL than the game ships with. 1 = latest from the manifest, or pin a version string.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FFX3_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] FidelityFX 3 counterpart of PROTON_FSR3_UPGRADE (used by the OptiScaler/upgrade path; not described in the fork's README table).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_FFX4_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] FidelityFX 4 counterpart of PROTON_FSR4_UPGRADE (used by the OptiScaler/upgrade path; not described in the fork's README table).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_XESS_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS] Download and use a newer Intel XeSS DLL than the game ships with. 1 = latest from the manifest, or pin a version string. XeSS runs on NVIDIA GPUs through its DP4a path.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_MLFG_UPGRADE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS] Enable MLFG (ML frame generation) together with FSR 4 >= 4.0.3. AMD-only; set together with PROTON_FSR4_UPGRADE.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_OPTISCALER
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS] Inject OptiScaler automatically so games can swap their upscaler (DLSS / FSR / XeSS) and add frame generation where the game has no option. The PROTON_<UPSCALER>_UPGRADE variables then choose the DLL versions. Config files live in <prefix>/drive_c/windows/system32/umu/.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_OPTISCALER_NAME
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] File name OptiScaler is injected as. Defaults to dxgi.dll; switch if the game already uses that DLL name.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_OPTISCALER_CONFIG
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] Semicolon-separated {section}.{option}={value} entries written into OptiScaler.ini (only options that already exist in the file). Changes persist until OptiScaler is upgraded and strip the file's comments. Example: Upscalers.Dx11Upscaler=fsr31;Upscalers.Dx12Upscaler=dlss

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_VKD3D_LOWLATENCY
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] Switch to the vkd3d-low-latency fork of vkd3d-proton (low-latency frame pacing for Direct3D 12 with a native Reflex implementation). Companion of PROTON_DXVK_LOWLATENCY for D3D12 titles.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_D7VK_DDRAW
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] Use ddraw.dll from the D7VK project for DirectX 7-and-older games instead of Wine's built-in ddraw.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_D7VK
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Use D7VK's ddraw implementation for DirectX 7-and-older games (GE spelling of PROTON_D7VK_DDRAW).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_D3D9
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Disable the D3D9 DLLs, for games that run better on another API.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_D3D12
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Disable the D3D12 DLLs, so a game with a DX11 fallback uses it instead of vkd3d-proton.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: LOW_LATENCY_LAYER
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Enable the low_latency_layer Vulkan layer (Korthos-Software), which provides Reflex-style latency reduction (VK_NV_low_latency2) on GPUs that lack it natively. Not needed on the proprietary NVIDIA driver.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: ENABLE_VKBASALT
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Load the vkBasalt post-processing Vulkan layer (sharpening, CAS, SMAA, LUTs). Configure it with VKBASALT_CONFIG_FILE.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PYROVEIL
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Enable the Pyroveil Vulkan layer, which patches broken shader/pipeline behaviour per game; the config name goes in PYROVEIL_CONFIG.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NATIVE_AGS
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-EM] Use AMD's proprietary AMD GPU Services binary instead of Proton's built-in one, and allow statically linked AGS. Mainly useful to enable HDR in some UE4 D3D11 games on AMD GPUs.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_WRITECOPY
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Simulate Windows copy-on-write (writecopy) semantics for loaded images (sets WINE_SIMULATE_WRITECOPY=1). Needed by some DRM/anti-cheat.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_WRITE_WATCH
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Disable memory write-watch support in ntdll. Can improve performance in a few specific games; only use after verifying the game runs without it.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_OLD_GL_STRING
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Limit the length of the GL extension string through driver overrides (sets MESA_EXTENSION_MAX_YEAR=2003 and __GL_ExtensionStringVersion=17700), for old OpenGL games that crash on very long strings.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_HIDE_INTEL_GPU
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Hide Intel GPUs from the game (sets WINE_HIDE_INTEL_GPU=1), for titles that break on Intel-specific code paths. Relevant on hybrid laptops with an Intel iGPU.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_HIDE_VANGOGH_GPU
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Hide the Steam Deck (Van Gogh) GPU from the game (sets WINE_HIDE_VANGOGH_GPU=1).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_XIM
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable the X Input Method (XIM) in Wine's X11 driver. Works around text-input/focus problems in a few games.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_SET_STEAM_DRIVE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Create a T: drive in the Wine prefix pointing at the Steam installation directory (counterpart of PROTON_SET_GAME_DRIVE's S: drive).

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_DLL_COPY
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma-separated list of built-in DLL globs Proton copies into the prefix (default: the DirectX / VC++ redistributable set, e.g. d3dcompiler_*.dll, xaudio*.dll, msvcp1*.dll). Setting it REPLACES that default list.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_X11_EXCLUSIVE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Under Wine-Wayland, run only this executable on winex11.drv while everything else stays on Wayland. Takes an exact basename (Launcher.exe) or a case-insensitive path fragment.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_WAYLAND_MONITOR
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Primary monitor for Wine-Wayland (sets WAYLANDDRV_PRIMARY_MONITOR). Auto-detected when unset.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_NO_STEAMINPUT
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-CachyOS / Proton-EM] Disable Steam Input support for the game. Proton-GE also sets it by itself in some controller-fallback cases; disable Steam Input for the game in Steam too.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_EMULATE_STEAMINPUT
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE / Proton-EM] Force Steam Input emulation on. Explicitly setting it also disables Proton-GE's automatic Sony-controller compatibility fallback.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_USE_PIPEWIRE
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] Use the native winepipewire.drv audio driver (enabled by default). Set 0 to fall back to winepulse.drv.

PROTON_ENV_VARS.name: PROTON_MEDIA_FORCE_GST
PROTON_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-CachyOS] Force the GStreamer media path. Fixes cutscene video/audio in some games.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_CPU_TOPOLOGY
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Overrides the CPU topology Wine reports to the game: 'N:i,j,k,...' exposes N logical CPUs, mapped onto host CPU indices i,j,k,.... Works around games that crash or refuse to launch on very high thread-count systems (Far Cry 4, Warhammer 40k: Space Marine and others cap out around 26-31 threads).

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_DISABLE_HARDWARE_SCHEDULING
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable Wine's hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling emulation path. Community workaround for titles (e.g. RTX Remix ports) that misbehave when this path is active on Linux.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_DISABLE_VULKAN_OPWR
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable Vulkan 'other process window rendering'. Works around issues on Wayland where the blit ends up one frame behind (compat string: noopwr).

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_INTEGER_SCALING
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable integer scaling in fullscreen mode, for sharp pixel-perfect upscaling instead of a blurry bilinear stretch.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_DO_NOT_CREATE_DXGI_DEVICE_MANAGER
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Workaround for video/audio playback issues in some games caused by incomplete IMFDXGIDeviceManager support (compat string: nomfdxgiman).

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_USE_KWIN_HACKS
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Enable KDE-specific windowing workarounds that can help on KDE Plasma older than 6.4 on Wayland or older than 6.6 on X11.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WAYLANDDRV_RAWINPUT
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-EM only, 10.0-1e+] Tunes mouse input under winewayland.drv. Set to 0 to fall back to accelerated (OS pointer-accel) input if raw input feels overly sensitive. On Proton-EM 10.0-2D+ you can instead pass any positive real number (e.g. 0.5) as a sensitivity multiplier for raw input — directly useful for dialing in mouse feel in FPS/aim-heavy titles run through the Wayland driver.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WAYLANDDRV_PRIMARY_MONITOR
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-EM only, 10.0-1b+] Explicitly names which monitor winewayland.drv should treat as primary (e.g. for fullscreen placement), since Wayland has no concept of a global primary monitor the way X11 does. Value is a compositor output name like 'eDP-1'. Shouldn't be needed on Proton-EM 10.0-25+.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_WAYLAND_HACKS
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-EM / Proton-CachyOS] Master toggle for winewayland.drv-specific workarounds. Set to 0 to disable them if they're the cause of an issue — one known case is critical-section timeouts in some launchers (e.g. EA App via the link2ea protocol) that clear up with this off.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEPULSE_FAST_POLLING
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Retired variable (no longer read by current Proton-CachyOS). Used to help eliminate crackling with the default PulseAudio driver, at the cost of rare crackling in some titles (e.g. God of War Ragnarok) with power-of-two quantum sizes like 512/768/1024. Kept here for older Proton/Wine builds.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEALSA_CHANNELS
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Select the channel count for the winealsa driver, or force-disable spatial audio. 2 disables spatial audio; 4/6/8 select 2-front+2-rear/5.1/7.1. Useful when dialogue or effects come out of the wrong speaker.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEALSA_SPATIAL
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Properly downmix spatial audio (including height channels) with winealsa. Only recommended if WINEALSA_CHANNELS alone still sounds wrong.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_BLOCK_HOSTS
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma- or semicolon-separated list of hosts Wine should refuse to connect to (max 16 hosts, 256 chars each). Useful for blocking telemetry/DRM phone-home hosts that cause launch hangs.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Enable AMD FSR upscaling inside Wine's fullscreen hack, so a game running at a lower fake resolution is upscaled to the monitor. Works in Vulkan games only (DXVK and VKD3D-Proton included) and needs the fullscreen hack, i.e. not under Wine-Wayland. Vendor-neutral, so it also runs on NVIDIA GPUs.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR_STRENGTH
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] FSR sharpening for WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR, 0-5. 0 is the sharpest, higher values sharpen less; 2 is AMD's recommended default and GE's default.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR_CUSTOM_MODE
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-GE] Fake screen resolution (WIDTHxHEIGHT) shown to the game while FSR upscales to the real mode. Useful for games that always render at native resolution.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINE_ENABLE_TIMEOUT_FIX
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: [Proton-DW (dwproton) only] Works around connection-timeout failures some setups hit launching live-service titles (originally documented for Genshin Impact / Zenless Zone Zero) that otherwise hang or fail to reach their servers.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEDEBUG
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Wine's own debug channel logging control. Syntax: [class][+|-]channel, comma separated, applied left to right; class is err, warn, fixme or trace. Wine's default (unset) is err+fixme on every channel. Base level (pick one): '-all' silences everything (fastest, normal play); 'fixme-all' = errors only; 'warn+all' adds warnings (recommended for debugging); '+all' turns on every class incl. trace — huge logs, very slow. Channel toggles add to the base, e.g. '-all,+loaddll' shows only DLL loads. Note: setting WINEDEBUG overrides the channel set PROTON_LOG=1 would otherwise pick.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEESYNC
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables the eventfd-based esync fast synchronization primitives in vanilla Wine/Lutris runners (not the Steam Proton wrapper, which is toggled via PROTON_NO_ESYNC instead). Reduces sync overhead vs the default server-side wineserver sync. Superseded by fsync/ntsync on kernels that support them, but still the common baseline on custom Wine builds without those patches.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEFSYNC
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables futex-based fsync synchronization in vanilla Wine/Lutris runners (requires a Wine build with the fsync patches and a reasonably recent kernel). Lower overhead than esync; takes priority over WINEESYNC when both a build supports fsync and this is set. Proton's equivalent toggle is PROTON_NO_FSYNC.

WINE_ENV_VARS.name: WINEDLLOVERRIDES
WINE_ENV_VARS.desc: Per-DLL override list controlling whether Wine uses its own built-in implementation or a native Windows DLL placed in the prefix, e.g. for staging in a DXVK/VKD3D DLL manually, or forcing a component to 'disabled' to work around a broken native/builtin implementation. Comma-separated 'dllname=mode' pairs; mode is n (native), b (builtin), n,b or b,n (try both, first listed wins), or empty (disabled).

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_D3D12_NV_SHADER_EXTN
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables experimental support for NVIDIA shader extensions in D3D12 titles (via VKD3D-Proton).

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_SET_NGX_DEBUG_OPTIONS
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma-separated key=value pairs forwarded to NVIDIA NGX's own debug-option system — the same mechanism as the Windows registry indicator keys. Commonly used to show an on-screen DLSS/DLSS-G indicator to confirm which preset/build is actually active.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: __NV_SIGNED_LOAD_CHECK
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Disables the NGX Core signature check that normally blocks loading non-NVIDIA-signed NGX features. Only disable this when you're confident every NGX feature DLL on the system is authentic — it exists to stop malicious NGX feature loading.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables DXVK-NVAPI's own Vulkan Reflex compatibility layer, for Reflex support in native-Vulkan titles (Portal RTX, Path of Exile 1/2, DOOM: The Dark Ages). Disabled by default even when installed, since it can interfere with other Vulkan apps that don't use Reflex. Formerly named PROTON_VKREFLEX.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DISABLE_DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Any non-empty value forcibly disables the Vulkan Reflex layer, overriding DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX_LAYER_LOG_LEVEL
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Log verbosity for the Vulkan Reflex compatibility layer specifically (separate from DXVK_NVAPI_LOG_LEVEL below).

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_LOG_LEVEL
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Log verbosity for DXVK-NVAPI itself; logging is off by default. 'info' logs the normal messages (incl. which DRS settings the game requested). 'trace' (newer releases) logs every entry point enter/exit — heavy on performance and log size.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_LOG_PATH
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Also write DXVK-NVAPI's log to nvapi.log / nvapi64.log / nvofapi64.log (per DLL) in this directory, in addition to console output. Needs LOG_LEVEL info or trace. Entries are appended to an existing file.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_DRIVER_VERSION
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Override the driver version DXVK-NVAPI reports to the game. Value is the version number with no dots, e.g. 47141 reports as driver 471.41.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_ALLOW_OTHER_DRIVERS
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Allow using DXVK-NVAPI without an NVIDIA GPU on the proprietary driver. Useful for exercising NVAPI D3D11 extensions on a non-NVIDIA GPU (e.g. Mesa/NVK).

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_DISABLE_ENTRYPOINTS
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: Comma-separated NVAPI entry point names to hide from the game — the game then sees those functions as unavailable. Workaround tool for titles that crash in one specific NVAPI path.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_FAKE_VKREFLEX
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: 1 = let Vulkan Reflex initialise successfully even when the dxvk-nvapi Vulkan Reflex layer is NOT installed (fake success, no latency reduction). 0 = never fake. Enabled automatically for DOOM: The Dark Ages to avoid its pink-tint bug. For real Reflex install the layer and use DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX_INJECT_SUBMIT_FRAME_IDS
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: VK Reflex layer: inject frame IDs (from NvAPI_Vulkan_SetLatencyMarker) into vkQueueSubmit* calls, helping the driver correlate submits with frames. Enables VK_KHR_present_id. May interfere with the game's own present IDs. Requires DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX_INJECT_PRESENT_FRAME_IDS
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: VK Reflex layer: inject frame IDs into vkQueuePresentKHR. Same caveats as ..._INJECT_SUBMIT_FRAME_IDS. Requires DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX_ALLOW_FALLBACK_TO_OOB_FRAME_ID
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: VK Reflex layer: when the game's latency markers carry no usable frame ID, the layer falls back to an out-of-band frame ID in submit and present calls (default on). 0 = disable that fallback. Only meaningful together with the INJECT_*_FRAME_IDS options. Requires DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX_ALLOW_FALLBACK_TO_PRESENT_FRAME_ID
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: VK Reflex layer: allow falling back to the present frame ID in vkQueueSubmit* calls (default on). 0 = disable that fallback. Only meaningful together with the INJECT_*_FRAME_IDS options. Requires DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX_ALLOW_FALLBACK_TO_SIMULATION_FRAME_ID
DXVK_NVAPI_ENV_VARS.desc: VK Reflex layer: allow falling back to the simulation frame ID in vkQueueSubmit* calls (default on). 0 = disable that fallback. Only meaningful together with the INJECT_*_FRAME_IDS options. Requires DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1.

NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.name: NVPRESENT_ENABLE_SMOOTH_MOTION
NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables VK_LAYER_NV_present, NVIDIA's driver-based frame-interpolation layer for Vulkan titles that don't have DLSS Frame Generation. RTX 50-series only.

NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.name: NVPRESENT_QUEUE_FAMILY
NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.desc: The layer presents from an asynchronous compute queue by default, which can conflict with some third-party overlays. Set to 1 to present from the graphics queue instead, at a small performance cost.

NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.name: NVPRESENT_LOG_LEVEL
NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.desc: Debug log verbosity for the NVPresent/Smooth Motion layer. Logs go to stderr by default; redirect with NVPRESENT_LOG_FILE. If nothing gets logged, check with VK_LOADER_DEBUG=layer whether the layer is loading at all.

NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.name: NVPRESENT_LOG_FILE
NVPRESENT_ENV_VARS.desc: Redirect NVPresent/Smooth Motion debug logging to this file instead of stderr.

SYS_ENV_VARS.name: VK_DRIVER_FILES
SYS_ENV_VARS.desc: Colon-separated list of Vulkan ICD manifest JSON files for the loader to use, overriding normal driver discovery. Modern replacement for the older VK_ICD_FILENAMES name (both are still accepted).

SYS_ENV_VARS.name: VK_LOADER_DEBUG
SYS_ENV_VARS.desc: Vulkan loader debug output channels. Each level shows ONLY that level (not cumulative), so list them, e.g. 'error,warn,info'. 'layer' shows which implicit/explicit layers are being discovered and loaded — the first thing to check when a Vulkan layer (NVPresent, MangoHud, gamescope's WSI layer, ...) doesn't seem to be active; 'driver' does the same for ICDs.

SYS_ENV_VARS.name: LD_PRELOAD
SYS_ENV_VARS.desc: Colon-separated list of shared libraries to load before all others for every process. Commonly used to preload an alternative allocator such as jemalloc or tcmalloc to reduce heap fragmentation/allocation overhead in some titles, or to inject overlay/hook libraries.

SYS_ENV_VARS.name: LD_BIND_NOW
SYS_ENV_VARS.desc: Force immediate (non-lazy) symbol binding at process start instead of lazy PLT resolution on first call. Slightly longer startup in exchange for removing small first-call resolution stutters later — mostly a micro-optimization.

SYS_ENV_VARS.name: __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME
SYS_ENV_VARS.desc: Forces which GLX vendor implementation libglvnd's vendor-neutral dispatch loads. Set to 'nvidia' to force the NVIDIA GLX path on hybrid/PRIME laptops where Mesa might otherwise be picked for the display GPU.

SYS_ENV_VARS.name: SDL_VIDEODRIVER
SYS_ENV_VARS.desc: SDL2 hint forcing which video backend SDL uses. 'wayland' forces native Wayland instead of SDL's default XWayland fallback; useful together with PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAMID
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: The Steam App ID of the game currently running inside gamescope.  Set automatically by the Steam client when launching through Steam.  gamescope reads this to look up the game's artwork for the overlay, apply per-game DRS presets on Steam Deck, and for FPS limit reporting in the Steam HUD.  You can set it manually in a Lutris command to give gamescope the right game context without going through Steam.  Example: STEAMID=730  (Counter-Strike 2)

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_HW_UPSCALE_FILTER
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Steam-specific override to select the upscale filter for gamescope via the Steam Settings UI path.  Maps to the same -F / --filter flag as the CLI 'Upscale Filter' option below but is written by the Steam client itself based on the per-game 'Scaling Filter' setting.  Setting it manually overrides whatever the Steam UI chose.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_HW_UPSCALE_FILTER=fsr

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_HW_UPSCALE_SHARPNESS
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Steam-specific sharpness override corresponding to the sharpness slider in Steam Settings -> Resolution.  Written by the client; override manually to bypass the UI.  Same 0-20 (FSR) / 0-5 (NIS) scale as the CLI --sharpness flag.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_HW_UPSCALE_SHARPNESS=5

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_VRR_ENABLED
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Steam client's per-game VRR toggle, written into gamescope's environment when you enable 'Allow Tearing' or 'VRR' in the Steam per-game settings.  Same effect as the CLI --adaptive-sync flag; the STEAM_ prefix just indicates it was set by the client rather than the user.  Override to force VRR on/off regardless of what the Steam UI shows.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_VRR_ENABLED=1

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_TEARING_SUPPORT
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Steam client flag advertising that the gamescope session supports tearing presents.  When set, the Steam HUD and the per-game settings panel show the 'Allow Tearing' toggle.  Set automatically in SteamOS; on desktop you may need to set it manually if you want Steam's tearing toggle to have any effect.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_TEARING_SUPPORT=1

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_DYNAMIC_REFRESH_SUPPORT
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Advertises VRR / dynamic refresh rate support to the Steam client so the per-game refresh-rate selector is shown.  Required on desktop gamescope if you want Steam's frame-rate-limit UI to work correctly.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_DYNAMIC_REFRESH_SUPPORT=1

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_LIMITER_RES
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Enables gamescope's own Steam-integrated FPS limiter UI.  When set to 1, the Steam overlay's frame-rate slider adjusts gamescope's -r cap in real time without restarting the game.  Set to 0 to manage the cap entirely via the CLI --framerate-limit flag below.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_LIMITER_RES=1

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_XWAYLAND_DISPLAY
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: The :DISPLAY number of the XWayland server gamescope started internally.  Set automatically by gamescope; forwarded to the game process so it can connect to gamescope's private XWayland rather than the host X server.  You normally never set this manually - it appears here so you can inspect or pin it when debugging multi-compositor scenarios.  Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_XWAYLAND_DISPLAY=:1

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: DISABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Disable switch of gamescope's Vulkan WSI layer (VkLayer_FROG_gamescope_wsi): the layer manifest's disable_environment, so DISABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI=1 stops the layer from loading at all. Use it when a game misbehaves with the layer (black video, bad swapchain) and ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI=0 is not enough.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_MANGOAPP_SOCKET_DISABLE
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Read by gamescope itself (set it on the gamescope process): stops gamescope from sending its per-frame data to mangoapp over the mangoapp socket. Debug/compat switch, e.g. when mangoapp is not draining the socket.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Toggles gamescope's Vulkan WSI (VK_layer) integration for the wrapped game. Proton sets this to 1 automatically when it detects it's running under gamescope, which lets the game present directly through gamescope's low-latency compositing path. Native (non-Proton) titles launched directly under gamescope do NOT get this set automatically, so setting it manually can improve latency for native Linux games. Conversely, some games show black/corrupted video playback or cutscenes with the WSI layer active - set to 0 as a workaround in that case. Community-sourced (gamescope issue #1958 / #1537), not in gamescope --help. Example: ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI=0 gamescope -- %command%

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_MULTIPLE_XWAYLANDS
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Requests a second, dedicated XWayland server from gamescope so overlay windows (Steam overlay, some anti-cheat/launcher UIs) run in their own XWayland instance separate from the game's - pair with the CLI --xwayland-count 2 flag below. Reduces overlay-related stutter/input issues in embedded gamescope sessions. Community-sourced session-script convention, not in gamescope --help. Example: STEAM_MULTIPLE_XWAYLANDS=1 gamescope --xwayland-count 2 -e -- steam -gamepadui

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_VRR_SUPPORTED
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Advertises to the Steam client that the current gamescope session is capable of VRR at all (distinct from STEAM_GAMESCOPE_VRR_ENABLED, which is the per-game on/off toggle). Needed on some desktop setups for Steam's VRR toggle to appear/function in per-game display settings. Community-sourced, not in gamescope --help. Example: STEAM_GAMESCOPE_VRR_SUPPORTED=1

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_WSI_MIN_IMAGE_COUNT
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Minimum swapchain image count the gamescope WSI layer reports to the game (default 3). Lower = less queued latency but more risk of stalls; higher = smoother under load. Also honours vk_wsi_override_min_image_count. Takes effect only with the WSI layer active (ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI).

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_WSI_ENSURE_MIN_IMAGE_COUNT
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Force the game's swapchain to use at least GAMESCOPE_WSI_MIN_IMAGE_COUNT images even if it asks for fewer.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_WSI_FORCE_BYPASS
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Ask gamescope to bypass composition (direct scanout) for this client whenever possible. Lowest latency path; may break overlays.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_WSI_FRAME_LIMITER_AWARE
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Tell gamescope the game's swapchain handles the gamescope frame limiter itself. Auto-enabled for DXVK >= 2.3 and vkd3d >= 2.12; set 1 for native Vulkan games that pace correctly, 0 to force gamescope-side limiting.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_DISABLE_ASYNC_FLIPS
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: DRM backend: never use async (tearing) page flips. Workaround for flicker/corruption with --immediate-flips on some drivers.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_FORCE_GENERAL_QUEUE
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Run gamescope's compositing on the general graphics queue instead of an async compute queue. Workaround for driver issues; may add latency.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_DISABLE_TIMERFD
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: Use the fallback sleep-based vblank timer instead of timerfd. Debug only.

GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.name: GAMESCOPE_LIFTOFF_CACHE_DISABLE
GAMESCOPE_ENV_VARS.desc: DRM backend: disable libliftoff's plane-allocation cache. Debug for direct-scanout / overlay-plane glitches.

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_FRAME_PACE
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc:
[dxvk-low-latency | DXVK-Sarek] Frame pacing mode — how CPU and GPU are synchronised. Overrides the dxvk.framePace config option.
max-frame-latency: stable latency in the GPU limit as long as render times are stable; higher latency but very smooth. Also what both forks fall back to when the value isn't recognised.
low-latency: the default in both forks. Lower latency in the GPU limit, fine-tunable via dxvk.lowLatencyOffset and dxvk.lowLatencyAllowCpuFramesOverlap.
min-latency: potentially the lowest latency, at the cost of fps — it stalls the GPU between frames. Generally not recommended; useful for tuning low-latency against, or for CPU-limited games.
low-latency-vrr-<Hz>: dxvk-low-latency ONLY — VRR-aware pacing at the given refresh rate. The fork's README suggests DXVK_FRAME_RATE=225 together with low-latency-vrr-235 on a 240 Hz VRR panel. Sarek does not implement this mode and will fall back to max-frame-latency.
Proton: proton-cachyos ships dxvk-low-latency behind PROTON_DXVK_LOWLATENCY=1 and DXVK-Sarek behind PROTON_DXVK_SAREK=1. Syntax: DXVK_FRAME_PACE=low-latency-vrr-235 DXVK_FRAME_RATE=225 %command%

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_ALL_CORES
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc: [DXVK-Sarek] Lets the pipeline compiler and the state-cache worker use every logical core instead of Sarek's default reduced thread count. Sarek targets older/weaker CPUs where saturating all cores during shader compilation starves the render thread, so it holds threads back by default. Worth setting on a modern many-core CPU where that reasoning no longer applies. Not present in upstream DXVK. Syntax: PROTON_DXVK_SAREK=1 DXVK_ALL_CORES=1 %command%

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_DISABLE_DYASYNC
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc: [DXVK-Sarek] Turns OFF dyasync (Dynamic Asynchronous Pipeline Compilation), which Sarek enables by default (dxvk.enableDyasync = True). With dyasync, a shader is compiled synchronously the first time it is seen; every later VARIANT of it (new blend mode, depth test, cull mode, render pass — same shaders) compiles in the background while DXVK draws with the closest already-compiled pipeline as a placeholder, then swaps it in. Safer than a classic async patch because something is always drawn, but it is still pipeline substitution — disable it for multiplayer titles with strict anti-cheat. Thread count is dxvk.numDyasyncThreads. Syntax: PROTON_DXVK_SAREK=1 DXVK_DISABLE_DYASYNC=1 %command%

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: DXVK_PERF_EVENTS
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc: [DXVK-Sarek] Enables VK_EXT_debug_utils so performance/debug events reach capture tools. Sarek hides the extension behind this variable because it adds real overhead in winevulkan — the fork logs a warning when it is on. Profiling only; leave unset for play. Syntax: PROTON_DXVK_SAREK=1 DXVK_PERF_EVENTS=1 %command%

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: D7VK_LOG_LEVEL
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc: [d7vk] Log level for the D3D7/6/5/3 translation layer. d7vk keeps its own logger separate from the DXVK D3D9 backend it sits on, so DXVK_LOG_LEVEL does NOT cover it — set both when tracing a DDraw-era title. Syntax: D7VK_LOG_LEVEL=debug D7VK_LOG_PATH=/tmp %command%

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: D7VK_LOG_PATH
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc: [d7vk] Directory for the d7vk log file. Same split as D7VK_LOG_LEVEL: independent of DXVK_LOG_PATH. Use 'none' to suppress the file entirely. Syntax: D7VK_LOG_PATH=/tmp %command%

FORK_ENV_VARS.name: VKD3D_LOW_LATENCY_OFFSET
FORK_ENV_VARS.desc:
[vkd3d-low-latency] Fine-tunes the low-latency frame pacer, in MICROSECONDS. Larger values start a frame later, which can improve responsiveness slightly; the fork defaults to 100us rather than 0 because it does not yet measure the blit cost. Clamped to 0-500 in the fork's code (values are parsed unsigned, so a negative number wraps — don't use one here, unlike DXVK's dxvk.lowLatencyOffset which genuinely accepts -10000..10000).
Only active when the game actually drives the pacer: it needs either the Nvidia Reflex API or a waitable DXGI swapchain. Confirm with PROTON_LOG=1 and look for the swapchain lines in the vkd3d log.
Proton-CachyOS: enable the fork with PROTON_VKD3D_LOWLATENCY=1; other Protons need d3d12.dll and d3d12core.dll replaced by hand. Syntax: VKD3D_LOW_LATENCY_OFFSET=100 %command%

OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.name: MANGOHUD
OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.desc: Load the MangoHud Vulkan layer for this process (alternative to the `mangohud` command prefix). Options come from MANGOHUD_CONFIG / MANGOHUD_CONFIGFILE or ~/.config/MangoHud/MangoHud.conf.

OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.name: MANGOHUD_CONFIG
OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.desc: Inline MangoHud options, comma separated (fps,cpu_temp,position=top-left). Overrides the config file for the keys it sets. Use the MangoHud builder (Extra Tools) to generate it.

OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.name: MANGOHUD_CONFIGFILE
OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.desc: Path of an explicit MangoHud config file instead of the per-user default.

OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.name: MANGOHUD_DLSYM
OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.desc: Hook dlsym so MangoHud also works with OpenGL / when injected via LD_PRELOAD. The `mangohud --dlsym` prefix sets this for you.

OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.name: VKBASALT_CONFIG_FILE
OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.desc: Path of the vkBasalt config file (default: ~/.config/vkBasalt/vkBasalt.conf). Pair with ENABLE_VKBASALT=1.

OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.name: VKBASALT_LOG_FILE
OVERLAY_ENV_VARS.desc: Write the vkBasalt log to this file instead of stderr.
